newsitem.title: GERMANY: Paris airport, SNCF in air cargo rail feeder talks.
newsitem.headline: Paris airport, SNCF in air cargo rail feeder talks.

text.p: Aeroports de Paris (ADP) said it is in talks with French national railway SNCF on developing an air cargo train feeder service within the next decade.
Alain Falque, ADP vice-president commercial, said the authority was looking into starting a rail cargo service for Charles de Gaulle airport, in particular to feed the Federal Express Europe hub.

"We strongly believe that the express freight market is the growth market in the cargo market. It is one of our development strategy sectors," he told Reuters at the launch of a Franco-German project to study improved air-rail links for passengers.
"We are in discussions with SNCF to see how we can develop this. It needs either high-speed trains or special cargo trains," he added.
"Our target (for operations) is 2000 to 2005," Flaque said.
Falaque said the new German Railways CargoSprinter train, capable of carrying air cargo containers, could be a model for a French air cargo train.
But he said the TGV cargo train idea was no longer a real candidate, without going into reasons for this view. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
